These do not address the definition of corporate loans, unearned income deferral, or portfolio-layer basis adjustments as described in Citigroup's disclosure.

Goldman Sachs' candidates discuss gross loan volumes in Private Banking and lending (gs_2024_7_D091) or the provision for credit losses driven by credit card portfolios and wholesale impairments (gs_2024_7_D056). Neither candidate addresses the specific accounting definition of corporate loans, unearned income deferrals, or basis adjustments central to Citigroup's disclosure.

JPMorgan Chase's candidates discuss drivers of Equity Markets net interest income decline (jpm_2024_7_D134) and Card income drivers including amortization of account origination costs (jpm_2024_7_D037). These topics are distinct from the corporate loan reporting definitions and unearned income treatments disclosed by Citigroup.

comparisons.peer_summary: Other net revenues were $1,262 million in 2024, an increase from $823 million in the prior year, primarily driven by lower mark-to-market losses on corporate loans and higher net interest income and fees.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup (C) and Morgan Stanley (MS) disclose specific details regarding the accounting treatment and performance drivers of their corporate loan portfolios, though they focus on different aspects. C explicitly defines its reporting basis by noting that corporate loans are reported net of unearned income (deferred origination fees) and excludes certain basis adjustments. MS provides performance context for its corporate loans, reporting that other net revenues increased primarily due to lower mark-to-market losses on corporate loans. While C quantifies the deferral adjustments ($969 million), MS highlights the P&L impact (lower losses contributing to revenue growth), indicating a shared focus on the valuation and economic reporting of corporate lending assets.

sentences.text: (3) Corporate loans are net of unearned income of $(969) million.

Unearned income on corporate loans primarily represents loan origination fees, net of certain direct origination costs, that are deferred and recognized as Interest income over the lives of the related loans.

Other net revenues were $1,262 million in 2024 compared with $823 million in the prior year, primarily due to lower mark-to-market losses on corporate loans, inclusive of hedges, and higher net interest income and fees on corporate loans.
